page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is a compute-oriented cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Hardware specifications include 64.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU features 33 MB of L3 cache, along with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. This instance has no direct-attached local storage and relies on network-attached storage over a 6 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear functional distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded performance. Single-core tests, such as Geekbench (960.0) and stress-ng CPU tests (1109.99), place the instance in the lower quartile among cloud hardware. Conversely, multi-threaded CPU execution reaches standard middle-tier levels, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core result of 23,557.71 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,426.0. Memory bandwidth remains in the average benchmark tier, delivering 74.54 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and supporting web serving throughput at 13.68 GB/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation offers qualitative cost efficiency for execution-heavy workloads that require high core counts without demanding extensive per-vCPU RAM reserves. The primary tradeoff is moderate per-core instruction throughput alongside complete reliance on remote block storage. Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is best suited for parallel processing workloads, software compilation, multi-threaded batch operations, Redis key-value caching, and general microservices backends.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is a compute-oriented x86_64 instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz across 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs. It comes provisioned with 64.0 GB of memory, representing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside a 33 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction set capabilities. The server does not include local disk storage, utilizing a 6 Gbps baseline network connection for remote storage and connectivity. Performance metrics demonstrate modest single-core throughput alongside balanced multi-core scaling, reaching average benchmark tiers in multi-threaded Geekbench tests, Redis SET operations, and static web serving. The resource configuration provides an efficient profile for parallel processing tasks that do not require high memory density per core. Optimal workload implementations include microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch execution jobs, and distributed application backends.
